skills.name: brandkit

skills.name: caveman

skills.name: code-review

skills.name: context7-mcp

skills.name: customize-opencode

skills.name: design-taste-frontend

Select automatically from that intent; ordinary UI and neutral landing pages use Impeccable.

skills.name: design-taste-frontend-v1

skills.name: domain-modeling

skills.name: doubt-driven-development
skills.description: Use ONLY for non-trivial high-risk or uncertain decisions involving auth/security, payments, destructive migrations/data loss, concurrency/correctness, difficult architecture, or unfamiliar high-impact code. Bounded fresh-context adversarial review. Ask the user before each cross-model escalation.

skills.name: emil-design-eng
skills.description: Emil Kowalski's motion and interaction-quality specialist. Automatically use to improve existing modal easing, transitions, micro-interactions, animation decisions or interaction polish. Supports the frontend owner; new animation construction uses animate.

skills.name: find-docs

skills.name: find-skills

skills.name: full-output-enforcement

skills.name: gpt-taste
skills.description: Cinematic GSAP/AIDA scrolltelling and gapless bento design. Use for an explicit motion-heavy/Awwwards request or this named style, not ordinary product UI.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.description: Use for explicitly requested interviews or substantial ambiguous work with unresolved requirements, terminology, or design decisions worth preserving in ADRs or a glossary. Simple fixes do not need grilling.

skills.name: grilling
skills.description: Supporting interview primitive. Use when called by grill-with-docs or wayfinder, or explicitly requested to stress-test a plan or decision. Investigate discoverable facts yourself; interview for unresolved human decisions.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Use when moving to a fresh session, switching models, context has become long/noisy, or another agent must continue. Preserve decisions, status, changed files, verification, unresolved issues, and artifact pointers.

skills.name: high-end-visual-design

skills.name: image-to-code
skills.description: Image-generation-first website implementation: generate references, analyze them, then build faithful code. Use for that explicit art-first workflow; supplied screenshot reconstruction belongs to the primary frontend workflow.

skills.name: imagegen-frontend-mobile
skills.description: Generate iOS/Android app-screen and flow concept images with coherent device framing. Images only; use for mobile visual concepts, not websites, responsive web coding or native app implementation.

skills.name: imagegen-frontend-web
skills.description: Generate website design-reference images, one horizontal image per section. Use for requested web comps/visual references, not ordinary UI coding or faithful reconstruction of an existing screenshot.

skills.name: impeccable
skills.description: Primary frontend engineering for ordinary UI/components, UX quality review and faithful supplied-screenshot reconstruction. Preserve project stack/brand; whole-app redesign and image-generation workflows have dedicated specialists.

skills.name: incremental-implementation
skills.description: Use for substantial or multi-file implementation in small reviewable slices: implement, verify, then continue. Avoid giant speculative changes. Trivial one-line changes need no artificial slicing or extra process.

skills.name: industrial-brutalist-ui
skills.description: Swiss industrial/blueprint or tactical CRT interface styling. Use for an explicitly requested brutalist/telemetry aesthetic, not all dashboards.

skills.name: karpathy-guidelines

skills.name: minimalist-ui
skills.description: Warm editorial, monochrome/pastel and flat UI styling. Use for that explicitly requested aesthetic or this named skill, not every minimalist product task.

skills.name: no-ai-slop
skills.description: Edit drafts into sharper, more human writing while preserving the writer's personal voice, or detect AI-slop patterns without rewriting. Use when the user wants a draft clearer, more direct, more opinionated, or less AI-sounding, or asks whether writing reads as AI.

skills.name: officecli
skills.description: Create, analyze, proofread, and modify Office documents (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) using the officecli CLI tool. Use when the user wants to create, inspect, check formatting, find issues, add charts, or modify Office documents.

skills.name: pick-ui-library
skills.description: Pick the right library for a given frontend task from a curated, opinionated list — numbers, OTP inputs, charts, command menus, virtualization, drag and drop, toasts, state, styling, and more. Only runs when explicitly invoked; it does not trigger on its own.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.description: Lazy senior dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, and a reply a busy human understands in one read. Use on any coding task (writing, fixing, refactoring, reviewing, choosing dependencies) and when the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", or complains about over-engineering or bloat. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.

skills.name: ponytail-audit
skills.description: Quality audit of a whole repo: bugs, security holes, what breaks under real load, risky code without tests, slow paths, and what to delete, merge or split. Ranked, each finding explained in plain English. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for "audit this codebase", "review the whole repo", "find bloat", "what can I delete", /ponytail-audit.

skills.name: ponytail-debt
skills.description: List every `shortcut:` comment (and older `ponytail:` ones) as a debt ledger. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for "ponytail debt", "what did ponytail defer", "list the shortcuts", /ponytail-debt.

skills.name: ponytail-gain
skills.description: Show ponytail's measured savings (code, cost, speed) from the benchmark. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-gain, "what does ponytail save", "ponytail impact".

skills.name: ponytail-help
skills.description: Quick reference for ponytail levels, skills and commands. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "how do I use ponytail".

skills.name: ponytail-review
skills.description: Quality review of a change: is the logic right, is it safe, does it hold under real load, is risky code tested, is it fast enough, and is every line needed. Reads the connected code, not only the diff. Each finding is explained in plain English. Use for "review this", "code review", "review the last commit", "review my PR", "is this over-engineered", /ponytail-review.
